overclaims: The accounting basis is unspecified, preventing a supported or contradicted monetary assessment.
checks.note: Excerpt, proposition, horizon and Meta qualifier are correct. Axis, horizon and outcome match the reviews. Citation e1 is accurate. Limitation 2 says the unspecified accounting basis prevents an assessment. The contract (interpretation_determines_result=false) doesn't support that, and it contradicts limitation 3, which says the result comes from the missing endpoint. 'Several relevant news pages' also overstates the failures: investing.com returned 403, and the JPMorgan page is research, not news, and was only partly readable.

Excerpt is verbatim. The proposition matches the compute-demand context. The H1 2026 target period appears in the interpretation. The rationale correctly reports >80% preleasing of capacity under construction in CBRE's primary North American markets, and Querétaro supply outpacing absorption in Q1. The publication-timing limitation is accurate (Aug 27 report covering H1). Citation excerpts, dates and relations match the frozen items. The outcome matches the reviews.

The proposition calls both inputs consensus estimates ('consensus estimates of about $186 billion… and $18.7 billion'). The speaker applies 'consensus' only to capex; revenue is just 'expected', and the contract notes it is attributed to Wells Fargo. The proposition therefore says more than the statement. The rationale is otherwise supported, though 'did not independently verify both' could suggest one input was verified; neither was. Citation e1 ($175B calendar-2026 guidance) is accurate. The outcome matches the reviews.
